title: Atom economy; Formulae and functional groups
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR01#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR01#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR01#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM10#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM10#N.3, OR01#N.5, AM10#N.5, OR01#N.9, AM10#N.9, OR01#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Skeletal formula
items.clue: A zig-zag of C–C bonds in which H on carbon is left out.

items.label: Displayed formula
items.clue: A drawing that shows every atom and every bond, including O–H.

items.label: Structural formula
items.clue: Shows the arrangement of atoms carbon by carbon, e.g. CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃.

items.label: Atom economy
items.clue: Percentage of the total mass of reactants that ends up in the desired product.

questions.stem: Which statement about atom economy and waste in an industrial process is correct?

options.text: The higher the percentage yield, the higher the atom economy, so less waste is produced.
Atom economy counts one molecule of each substance, so the coefficients do not affect it.
A process with an atom economy of 100% produces no waste of any kind at all.
The lower the atom economy, the greater the proportion of reactant mass that becomes waste.

questions.explanation: The mass not in the desired product ends up in by-products, so atom economy and waste are inversely related.

questions.stem: Propan-2-ol has the molecular formula C₃H₈O. Which statement about the formula C₃H₈O is correct?

options.text: It is the molecular formula only, since an empirical formula is simpler.
It is a structural formula, as it lists every atom present.
It identifies propan-2-ol, since no other compound has this formula.
It is both the molecular and the empirical formula of propan-2-ol.

questions.explanation: 3, 8 and 1 have no common factor, so the ratio is already the simplest. Empirical = molecular here.

questions.stem: Which reaction has an atom economy of 100% for the product named?

options.text: CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g), making calcium oxide
H₂SO₄(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SO₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l), making sodium sulfate
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g), making sulfur trioxide
Any reaction that is carried out with a 100% yield

questions.explanation: This reaction has a single product, so every reactant atom ends up in it: 100%.

questions.stem: Which compound contains an ester group?

options.text: CH₃COOH
CH₃CH₂OCH₃
CH₃COOCH₃
CH₃COCH₂CH₃

questions.explanation: The C=O carbon is bonded to an O that is bonded to a carbon: –COO–. This is methyl ethanoate, an ester.

questions.stem: Hydrogen is manufactured by reacting methane with steam: CH₄(g) + H₂O(g) → CO(g) + 3H₂(g). In one batch, 16.0 kg of methane gave 4.80 kg of hydrogen. What is the atom economy for producing hydrogen by this reaction? (Aᵣ: H 1.0, C 12.0, O 16.0)
questions.explanation: 3 × 2.0 ÷ (16.0 + 18.0) × 100 = 6.0 ÷ 34.0 × 100 = 17.6%. The products total is the same: 28.0 + 6.0 = 34.0. The rest of the mass ends up as CO.

questions.stem: Two bottles both contain a liquid with the molecular formula C₂H₄O₂. Liquid X boils at 118 °C and turns blue litmus red. Liquid Y boils at 32 °C and is neutral. Which explains this?

options.text: X and Y must be the same compound, so one of the two samples must be impure.
X's molecules are heavier, so more energy is needed to separate them.
X is CH₃COOH, with a carboxyl group; Y is HCOOCH₃, with an ester group.
X is CH₃COOH, a carboxylic acid; Y is CH₃CHO, an aldehyde with no acidic O–H group.

questions.explanation: Same atoms, different structures. X's carboxyl O–H makes it acidic and lets its molecules hydrogen-bond, so it boils far higher. The ester has no O–H.
